test_title: PYST 8: Selection Post (Higher Secondary Level) - Quant (Held On 02 Aug, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: maths
question: A shopkeeper earns 70% profit on selling an article. If he increases the selling price by Rs. 338, the profit becomes 83%. Find the cost price.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Initial profit = 70% and Final profit = 83%

Difference in profit percentage = 83% − 70% = 13%

This 13% difference corresponds to the increase in Selling Price of Rs. 338.

∴ 13% of Cost Price = 338

∴ 100% of Cost Price = (338 ÷ 13) × 100 = 26 × 100 = Rs. 2600

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 2600.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: Initial Profit = 70%, New Profit = 83%, Increase in SP = Rs. 338

Formula: Selling Price (SP) = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3bd4df534863f5f08c7f8378d07ae309557dd849145c4ab03c37b11012e4bc0.png] 

⇒ Let the Cost Price (CP) of the article be Rs. x.

⇒ Initial Selling Price (SP₁) = 170% of x = 1.70x

⇒ New Selling Price (SP₂) = 183% of x = 1.83x

⇒ According to the question: SP₂ − SP₁ = 338

⇒ 1.83x − 1.70x = 338

⇒ 0.13x = 338

⇒ x = 338 ÷ 0.13

⇒ x = 2600

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 2600.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss Basics

Profit occurs when SP > CP. Profit % = [(SP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100. Loss occurs when CP > SP. Loss % = [(CP − SP) ÷ CP] × 100.

Relation between CP and SP

When profit is p%, SP = CP × (100 + p) ÷ 100. When loss is l%, SP = CP × (100 − l) ÷ 100.

Marked Price and Discount

Marked Price (MP) is the price labeled on the article. Discount is always offered on MP. SP = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100.</p
